svg.text: K1b Cutting force without a ram: a bought lever dicer on a stand over T0
The arm presses the lever pad down; the lever multiplies 300 N to about 2 kN. The force stays inside the dicer frame.
bought catering push-dicer (Vollrath InstaCut / Nemco class)
grids 6 / 10 / 20 mm, wedger-corer, fry cutter, ricer plate 3 mm
arm 300 N × lever 7 ≈ 2.1 kN at the pusher · 2 onions: 2 loads, 50 s
stand: 4 legs, 320 × 320 span, grid 30 mm above the vessel rim
bowl on T0 (or a pot on H1 / H2)

g.text: root plate stays on the grid

svg.text: RICING potatoes in their skins (P2: skins stay on the plate)
3 L pot with hot milk and butter on T0

g.text: 1/6 Load: the dicer stands over the bowl on T0; the tongs lay two peeled onion halves flat side down into its chamber
2/6 Press: the arm pushes the lever pad down with 300 N; the pusher drives the onion through the 6 mm grid with about 2 kN
3/6 Release: dice fall into the bowl; the root plate stays on the grid
4/6 Second load: two more halves; their press pushes the old root plate through — 2 onions in about 50 s
5/6 Ricing (P2): boiled potatoes go in with their skins; pressed through the 3 mm plate, the flesh drops into the milk
6/6 The skins stay on the plate as a mat and are knocked off into the dump slot; no peeling needed for mash
